  "schema_version": "0.1",
  "kind": "claim",
  "claim": "On the prior project's instrument the red particle's emission was strongest through emission wheel position 3, measured by running the same particle through all four single-band positions on 2026-09-06.",

  "source": "prior_run:agentic-microscope@filters-2026-09-06",

  "source_ref": "src_prior_filter_records",
  "validity_conditions": "MEASURED RATHER THAN CHOSEN, and the controls are what make it quantitative. The four positions gave 0.1, 1.6, 362.1 and 62.3 ADU. A6 needs the wavelength actually collected and that is the band of position 3, not a peak inside it. CORROBORATED INDEPENDENTLY ON THIS BENCH. Today's E2 observation, particles_show_on_the_green_605_path, puts this bottle's emission in the same band on this instrument. Two observations, two instruments, two projects. The prior project's numbers are not borrowed for that -- the agreement is what makes borrowing unnecessary. WHICH WHEEL is not settled by this. emission_wheel_camera_mapping is E5 `operator_recall:` and says the first wheel serves red, `probably`. This entry is about positions WITHIN a wheel and neither confirms nor contradicts it. THE POSITION IS A STRING, NOT A NUMBER, and the schema caught me writing it as one. 5.3's own examples of a nominal designation are `20x` 대물렌즈, `1.5x` 줌 and 필터 위치 `3` -- this exact case. A slot index names WHICH SLOT and asserts no quantity, so it has no uncertainty and no place in numbers[]. I reached for `precision: exact` to express that, which the enum does not have, and the absence is the argument: a value needing `exact` is a value that should not be in numbers[] at all.",

      "note": "the reading was reported as 20 degrees Celsius. The store carries kelvin because the unit registry is multiplicative -- si_factor and a dimension vector cannot express an offset unit, so Celsius cannot enter it at all. 293 K rather than 293.15 K: the exact conversion would claim five figures from a reading given to the nearest degree, and the 0.15 K it drops is far inside the resolution of the reading."
    }
  ],
  "validity_conditions": "The room as of 2026-09-17, operator read off a thermometer. CORRECTED 2026-09-19: this entry used to reason that the value could not be a setpoint because nothing actuates the temperature. That premise was false and the conclusion was right. The room IS held, by continuous air conditioning; what is not actuated is the SAMPLE, and the entry had collapsed the two. The grade never rested on that argument: 20 C is a value someone READ, which 12 grades differently from a setpoint, and a room value applied to the sample is not a measurement of the sample. A right answer standing on a wrong reason is the thing that rots, and as written the sentence asserted that this room is uncontrolled. The controlled room does not shrink the sample question, it ISOLATES it: with the room held, whatever still moves at the sample is local -- illumination, a contacting objective, the stage -- and those have their own open gap. Do not read 'the room is controlled' as 'temperature is handled'. WHERE the thermometer sits is now stated rather than inferred (no_thermometer_at_the_sample): it reads the room, and how far that is from the sample and how well the two track are both unknown. A plan needing the viscosity or the thermal energy AT THE SAMPLE stands on that gap rather than on this entry. Water's viscosity moves by roughly two percent per kelvin, so in explore mode a drift of about a kelvin does not move a decade and can be ignored, while in confirm mode it cannot.   "validity_conditions": "THE SCOPE IS AN INSTANCE, AND IT LIVES IN `subject`, NOT IN `validity`.   "validity_conditions": "THIS IS NOT A LIMIT AND MAY NOT BE USED AS ONE. 'Keep it under 20 percent' is the sentence someone lifts out of an entry and uses to parameterise a laser, and three separate rules forbid that: safety limits live in a file a person writes and in deterministic code (P0, 2.1 rule 7), they do not transfer (10.3 rule 4), and the grade forbids it on its own -- an E5 may not parameterise an irreversible action without a person's individual approval, and raising laser power onto a sample is irreversible to the sample. Anyone needing a bound writes one in envelope/safety.json after confirming it physically. Three things this says less than it appears to. It is RECALLED, not read, which is why it is E5 while the neighbouring instrument facts are E3. It is a DETECTION BOUND and not a zero: 'did not notice' was measured by unrecorded means, and 'no heating below 20 percent' is a stronger claim than was made. And 20 PERCENT IS A DIAL READING, not a power: a percentage of an unstated maximum is not a quantity, and writing it into numbers[] would not make it one -- the same ruling that keeps a nominal magnification out of numbers[], wearing different clothes. It does not close the heating gap. A measured heating rate is still absent, and a gap that looks satisfied by an E5 recollection is a false absence running backwards. {
  "entry_id": "working_distance_is_measured_to_the_coverslip",
  "schema_version": "0.1",
  "kind": "claim",
  "claim": "The catalogue working distances for the objectives on this nosepiece are measured from the front element to the coverslip's lens-facing surface, not to the sample plane. This is inferred from two facts the store already holds; no document was read that says it.",
  "subject": [
    {
      "kind": "device",
      "id": "nosepiece"
    }
  ],
  "inputs": ["working_distance", "coverslip_thickness"],
  "source": "computed:working_distance_versus_coverslip",
  "grade": "E4",
  "grade_tag": "computed",
  "source_ref": "src_store_derivation",
  "validity_conditions": "THE INFERENCE, AND IT IS AN INFERENCE. Three of the six objectives have a catalogue working distance SHORTER than the coverslip this laboratory mounts on: 60x Oil at 150 um (objective_mrd71670), 100x Oil at 130 um (objective_mrd71970), and 40x WI from 160 um (objective_mrd77400), against coverslip_thickness 170 um (coverslip_thickness_in_use, E3, operator_read). If the catalogue measured to the SAMPLE PLANE, then at focus the front element of those three would sit nearer the sample than the glass is thick -- inside the coverslip. It cannot. So the catalogue measures to the coverslip's lens-facing surface, and the distance from front element to sample is the working distance plus the coverslip thickness.\n\nRECORDED AS AN INFERENCE OR NOT AT ALL, which is how task 021 put it and why this is E4 rather than E3. Nothing was read. Two E3 facts and one impossibility give it, and 5.3 caps a consequence at E4 however good its inputs are. A later reading of the Nikon catalogue that states the convention outright would supersede this at E3; a measurement on this bench would do better still.\n\nWHAT IT IS NOT NEEDED FOR. Not for the focus ceiling. Task 021 recorded the person's correction of an over-built argument: a lens is at its working distance when it is in focus, by definition, so `do not pass the working distance` means `do not pass focus` whichever surface the catalogue measured from. The convention does not enter that rule and the ceiling did not wait on it.\n\nWHAT IT IS NEEDED FOR. Anything computing an absolute Z in stage coordinates from the coverslip geometry -- where the sample plane sits relative to a focused objective, how far a stage may travel before the element meets glass, and any conversion between a focus position and a depth in the sample. Those need the plus-170 and get it wrong silently without this.\n\nWHY THIS ONE DERIVES AND declared_versus_inferred_temperature DOES NOT. Both are conclusions this store reasoned to rather than read, and both are `computed:` at E4. The difference is what they rest on: this rests on two QUANTITIES the store carries as numbers, `working_distance` and `coverslip_thickness`, so `inputs` resolves and check 62 can verify the grade. That entry rests on CLAIMS carrying no numbers, so nothing composes. Same source kind, two different shapes -- which is the gap raised with manager-librarian under task 020.",
  "date": "2026-09-20",
  "supersedes": null,
  "conflict_with": [],
  "curated_by": "kyuhwan"
}
